questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite angle theta is 8 cm and the hypotenuse is 17 cm. What is sin(theta)?
questions.explanation: sin(theta) = opposite / hypotenuse = 8/17. The adjacent side (15 cm by Pythagoras) is not needed for sine.

questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the adjacent side to angle theta is 5 cm and the hypotenuse is 13 cm. What is cos(theta)?
In a right-angled triangle, the opposite side is 6 cm and the adjacent side is 8 cm. What is tan(theta)?
questions.explanation: tan(theta) = opposite / adjacent = 6/8 = 3/4. A common mistake is to use the hypotenuse (10 cm) instead.

questions.stem: Which mnemonic helps you remember the three trigonometric ratios?
questions.explanation: SOH CAH TOA: Sin = Opposite/Hypotenuse, Cos = Adjacent/Hypotenuse, Tan = Opposite/Adjacent.

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm. The angle theta is opposite the side of length 3. What is sin(theta)?
questions.explanation: sin(theta) = opposite / hypotenuse = 3/5. The hypotenuse is always the longest side (5 cm).
